body.p: Reconsideration of the Application is respectfully requested. I. Status of the Claims

Claims 24 and 37 are amended herein. Claim 28 is canceled. Claims 25-27, 29-36, and 38- 44 are as previously presented. Support for the amendments can be found in the Specification, specifically Paragraphs [0043] and [0044]. No new matter has been added and claims 24-27 and 29-44 are pending.
II. Double Patenting Rejection

Claims 24-27, 29-33, and 35-36 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory obviousness- type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 12-14 and 19 of copending Application No. 16/896,099 in view of US Patent No. 9,259,156 to Warner et al. ("Warner").
Claims 37-44 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-3 of copending Application No. 16/896,099.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with Examiner's analysis of the cited reference. Applicant further respectfully requests that Examiner hold this rejection in abeyance until there is an indication of allowable subject matter. Applicant will, at that time, consider filing a Terminal Disclaimer. See, e.g., MPEP 804.
III. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103

Claims 24-35 and 37-43 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent No. 10,398,346 to Ghoraani et al. ("Ghoraani") in view of U.S. Patent No. 9,259,156 to Warner et al. ("Warner"). Claims 36 and 44 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Ghoraani in view of Warner and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 6,773,402 to Govari et al. ("Govari").
Applicant respectfully disagrees. Ghoraani does not show, disclose, or suggest at least:
a tubular shaft having a proximal end and a distal end, the tubular shaft
extending along a longitudinal axis;
an expandable basket assembly coupled to the distal end of the tubular shaft,
the basket assembly comprising:
a plurality of splines configured to bow radially outward from the
longitudinal axis; and
a plurality of electrodes attached to the plurality of splines;
as recited in Claim 24. This feature is shown in FIG. 2 of the present Application, reproduced below.

Rather, Ghoraani discloses "a means to guide the placement of an MPDC in the atria to locate the AF sources (rotors and foci)," (Ghoraani at 0066, MPDC meaning a "Multi-Pole Diagnostic Catheter") wherein, "guidance of MPDC placement is provided by the present solution via an AF ablation target map." (Ghoraani at 0066). The "multi-polar catheter" as disclosed in Ghoraani at 0028 is not the same as the basket catheter recited in Claim 24.
Rather, Ghoraani discourages use of a basket catheter and emphasizes the "limitations of the basket catheter" (Ghoraani at 0003). Specifically, Ghoraani states

"Moreover, regions such as the left atrial appendage are incompletely covered by the basket catheter. As a result, the basket catheter does not record arrhythmia substrates involving these structures. Additionally, basket catheter mapping does not permit immediate correlation of activation times to precise anatomical sites."
(Ghoraani at 0003, emphasis added).
Accordingly, Ghoraani discourages against the use of a basket catheter as recited in Claim 24.

Applicant further submits Warner does not cure the deficiencies of Ghoraani. Although Warner contemplates a "basket catheter", as explained above, Ghoraani discourages against using a basket catheter. Therefore, a person of ordinary skill in the art would not look to modify disclosure of Ghoraani with the disclosure of Warner to arrive at the claimed invention. That is, there is no motivation or suggestion to combine and therefore no prima facie obviousness can be established. Accordingly, Ghoraani, alone or in combination with Warner, does not show, disclose, or suggest all of the features of claim 24 for this reason alone.

Applicant further submits that Govari does not cure the deficiencies of Ghoraani or Warner. Rather Govari contemplates a body electrode attached to the body which is patentably distinguishable from the basket catheter features recited in Claim 24. Accordingly, Ghoraani, alone or in combination with Warner and Govari, does not show, disclose, or suggest all of the features of claim 24.

Where all claimed features are not shown or described in the relied upon prior art, Office personnel (as noted in MPEP § 2141) must explain why the differences between the relied-upon prior art and the claimed invention would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art. Absent a narrative explaining how the combination of Ghoraani in view of Warner and further in view of Govari would be used by one of ordinary skill to arrive at all claimed features, claim 24 is patentable over Ghoraani in view of Warner and further in view of Govari. Applicant further submits that claim 37 is allowable for this additional reason.

In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 24 and 37 are in condition for allowance. Applicant further submits that all claims depending from claims 24 and 37 are allowable at least for their dependence on an allowable claim. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims are in condition for allowance and requests the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be removed.
VI. Fees

This Response is filed within 4 months of the 10 April 2023 Office Action. A one-month extension of time fee is believed due. No claims fees are believed to be due. No additional fees are believed to be due. Applicant nonetheless authorizes the Commissioner to charge deposit account No. 20-1507 for any fees deemed due to keep the Application pending or credit any overpayment.

It is believed the Application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is respectfully requested to contact the undersigned if there are any remaining issues which can be resolved by a Supplemental or Examiner's Amendment.
